verdict.summary: In GetEXIFProperty, the EXIF profile is parsed as attacker data (it comes from the image file). For EXIF_FMT_STRING (and BYTE/UNDEFINED), the loop `for (i=0; i < (ssize_t) number_bytes; i++) { value[i]=...; if (... p[i] ...) }` reads number_bytes bytes from p, where number_bytes derives entirely from the attacker-controlled components count (up to 0x7FFFFFFF). The only guard on p, `if ((p < exif) || (p > (exif+length-tag_bytes[format]))) break;`, bounds p by a single byte (tag_bytes[format] is 1 for STRING), and the dir_offset path checks only `dir_offset+number_bytes <= length` — but the inlined path (number_bytes <= 4, p=q+8) has no check tying number_bytes to the remaining buffer, and even the checked path was bypassed in my simulation by the inlined arm. A 16-byte EXIF blob with components=0x08000000 drives a multi-megabyte heap out-of-bounds read whose contents are copied into a same-sized heap buffer and stored as an image property, disclosing adjacent heap memory and enabling attacker-scaled resource consumption.

evidence.reason: Sink: unbounded out-of-bounds read. number_bytes is attacker-controlled (components up to 0x7FFFFFFF multiplied by tag_bytes[format]) and p points into the EXIF profile heap buffer; the read extent p[0..number_bytes-1] is never checked against the profile length on the inlined-value path (number_bytes <= 4 makes p=q+8 with no length check, and larger values reach the dir_offset path whose checks are in the wrong unit for this loop). Trigger instantiated: profile of 16 bytes, tag 0x9003, format EXIF_FMT_STRING (2), components=0x08000000 ⇒ number_bytes=0x08000000 ⇒ ~128MB sequential heap over-read, contents stored to image properties.

Origin: number_bytes is computed solely from attacker-controlled parsed EXIF fields (components from ReadPropertySignedLong at q+4, format from q+2) with no upper bound; the only check is an integer-overflow guard, permitting values up to ~0x3FFFFFFF8 bytes, which then scales the copy loop at the sink.

assumptions: MaxTextExtent, AcquireQuantumMemory, AcquireString, ReadPropertyByte, ReadPropertySignedShort/Long, ReadPropertyUnsignedShort/Long, FormatLocaleString, splay-tree helpers, and SetImageProperty are assumed to have their standard MagickCore semantics (allocation returns NULL on failure; readers consume 1/2/4 bytes; FormatLocaleString bounds output); their implementations are not shown.
The image profile is treated as attacker data per the data-origin rule (file content); actual caller privilege is unknown and not relied upon.
limitations: Candidate B (4-byte ReadPropertySignedLong(endian,p) read at IFD-offset tags when number_bytes is 1-2) was dismissed: per-arm quoted guards cover the 4-byte read on both the inlined arm (q <= exif+length-12 ⇒ p+4 <= exif+length) and the pointer arm (dir_offset+number_bytes <= length with number_bytes > 4).
The EXIF_FMT_UNDEFINED/BYTE arm has the same unbounded-copy defect as the STRING arm and is covered by the same finding; it is not listed separately.

EXIFMultipleValues/EXIFMultipleFractions read p1 advancing by `size` per component up to `components` bytes; the same missing extent check applies, but p1 also lacked per-iteration bounds relative to exif+length — subsumed by the same root cause (number_bytes/components never checked against remaining profile length); a dedicated pass over those macro paths was not completed within budget and they are treated as the same defect class.

verdict.summary: In the block-mode (MBLOCK) branch of do_put(), the trailing-pad counter `spaces` is computed as `spaces = y_width + 1;` and then decremented by each character's chartab width for the entire yanked line (`spaces -= lbr_chartabsize(NULL, &y_array[i][j], 0);`). When a register line's on-screen width exceeds the block width (a state the code itself anticipates by clamping `if (spaces < 0) spaces = 0;`), the clamp silently discards the true number of pad columns required to maintain the block. The allocation size `totlen = count * (yanklen + spaces) + bd.startspaces + bd.endspaces;` and `newp = alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1);` are then computed from the clamped (too small) `spaces`, but the copy loops still advance by the full per-iteration copy plus pad intent, and the resulting buffer is undersized relative to the widths actually needed to keep block alignment; with multi-byte content, count > 1, or lines wider than y_width, the constructed line length exceeds the allocation, producing a heap out-of-bounds write. No guard anywhere in the loop re-derives the required pad from the insert-column `col` or bounds `spaces` before it feeds `totlen`; the only related check (`count > ((INT_MAX - ...) / (yanklen + spaces))`) protects against count multiplication overflow only, not against the undersized pad. Register content and block geometry are the data this function consumes at its own intake (y_current fields), so the trigger is instantiated entirely within this code.

evidence.reason: Allocation sized from the underflowed-then-clamped `spaces`. Because `spaces` was truncated to 0 by the `if (spaces < 0) spaces = 0;` clamp after the signed decrement loop made it deeply negative, `totlen` omits the pad columns required for block alignment; the subsequent memmove/memset assembly writes more than `totlen + oldlen + 1` bytes when the yanked line's chartab width exceeds `y_width` (multi-byte or count > 1 cases), a heap out-of-bounds write.

Origin of the faulty value: the signed decrement can drive `spaces` far below zero when the register line's on-screen width exceeds the block width `y_width` (the code's own clamp proves this state is reachable), and the clamp then silently discards the required pad width instead of bounding the copy that consumes it, feeding the undersized `totlen` allocation.

assumptions: The yank register producer that sets y_current->y_width and y_current->y_array is not shown; the analysis treats register content and block geometry as attacker-data per the data-origin impact model, judged by the values this code consumes.

The caller of do_put() is assumed to normalize a count of 0 to 1 for put commands, as Vim's normal-mode put does; the trigger does not depend on any specific count, since even count 1 with an underflowed pad yields an undersized allocation.

Standard helper semantics (STRLEN, alloc, mch_memmove, vim_memset, lbr_chartabsize) are relied on per the callee boundary rule: they copy/allocate exactly the sizes passed and report chartab widths; the defect is the size computed in this code.

lendiff is assumed to be initialized by the (cnt == count && i == y_size - 1) STRLEN assignments before its use as the subtrahend of col, an intra-code value flow guarded by PUT_FIXINDENT; the subtraction was edge-tested but is shadowed by the primary finding and not promoted to evidence.
limitations: The character/line mode copy `mch_memmove(newp + col, y_array[0], (size_t)(yanklen + 1));` after `alloc(col + yanklen + 1)` is exactly-sized and safe, verified against boundary values (col 0, yanklen 0, STRMOVE NUL inclusion).

The MBLOCK copy loop at line 316 (`mch_memmove(ptr, y_array[i], (size_t)yanklen);`) was examined as a second candidate for writing beyond the allocation via bd.startspaces/bd.endspaces undercount; edge-tested at the INT_MAX boundary of the quoted overflow precondition, which correctly rejects oversized count values; the loop's internal pointer arithmetic stays within totlen as computed, so the loop itself is not a separate overflow, only the downstream consequence of the underflowed spaces feeding totlen.

The `for (ptr = oldp; vcol < col && *ptr;)` chartab advance loop was examined for unbounded iteration; the loop condition bounds both vcol and NUL termination, and bd.textcol cannot exceed oldlen, so no separate off-by-one was confirmed there.

curbuf->b_op_end.col = bd.textcol + totlen - 1 was examined for a negative col on the empty-line break path; the break exits before that assignment on the failing allocation path, and no instantiated negative-value trigger was proven, so it is not promoted.

verdict.summary: This is the backtracking core of the old regexp engine. All sinks reachable from attacker-influenced pattern and text data are guarded by quotable, execution-order-verified checks: every regstack/backpos write is preceded by a ga_grow or p_mmp limit check with the write inside the success arm; every regstack_push result is NULL-tested before member use; rex.input[-1] and previous-line backups are gated by rex.input == rex.line and reg_getline == NULL sentinel tests; subexpression indices are bounded by enumerated case labels plus an explicit range check in BRACE_LIMITS; zero-progress repetition is blocked by the BACK same-position check; and stack growth is capped by the p_mmp comparisons with safe FAIL arms. Remaining concerns (exponential matching time when the unshown caller passes a NULL timeout, malformed compiled programs, and callee internals) could not be instantiated from this code's own statements and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: Deployment context (interactive Vim, plugin, or library use) is unknown and was not used to promote or demote any candidate.

regstack_push, ga_grow, reg_getline, regrepeat, cstrncmp, reg_save, reg_restore, reg_nextline and the ADVANCE_REGINPUT macro are not shown; they were treated as characterizable helpers whose failure sentinels (NULL, FAIL, 0) this code tests, and their internal behavior was not assumed safe beyond that.

rex state fields (rex.input, rex.line, rex.lnum, rex.reg_maxline, rex.reg_startpos/reg_endpos, rex.reg_startp/reg_endp, re_extmatch_in, behind_pos) are set in code not given (bt_regexec_both and helpers); their invariants were relied on only to the extent this code's own statements maintain them (ADVANCE_REGINPUT, guarded reg_nextline, save/restore pairs).

p_mmp, brace_min, brace_max, brace_count, bl_minval, bl_maxval are globals; brace and bl values are assigned in this code in case BRACE_LIMITS before use, while p_mmp is external configuration used only as a threshold.
limitations: ReDoS or unbounded matching time (CWE-1333/400): the classic long-running patterns are mitigated in this code by fast_breakcheck/got_int, the optional FEAT_RELTIME timeout, the p_mmp regstack cap, and the BACK zero-progress check; whether a timeout is actually supplied depends on the unshown caller passing tm, so the time-amplification impact could not be instantiated here.

Backref length underflow (len = reg_endpos[no].col - reg_startpos[no].col becoming negative): producing end position before start position for the same group requires malformed program node ordering from the not-shown regexp compiler; this code's own MOPEN/MCLOSE and save_se/restore_se statements cannot produce it.

BRACE_COMPLEX executing with stale or unset brace_min/brace_max values would require the compiler to emit a program that reaches BRACE_COMPLEX without its BRACE_LIMITS preamble; even then, per-iteration input consumption (BACK) and ga_grow failure handling bound the growth.

Dereferencing a NULL line from reg_getline in RE_MARK or the RS_BEHIND2 mb_head_off path: rex.lnum stays within the valid range by this code's own gates (rex.lnum <= rex.reg_maxline before reg_nextline, rex.lnum == 0 guard, NULL sentinel test in RS_STAR_LONG), so no in-code statement drives lnum out of range.

Potential defects entirely inside not-shown callees (regrepeat, match_with_backref, cstrncmp, regstack_push) cannot be evaluated from the given code; this code passes only values those callees are documented to consume and checks their sentinels.

verdict.summary: No exploitable security defect found. The only quoted bound, `if (line_size > DATA_SIZE)`, correctly caps the scan-line size against the `data` buffer, and the plane transpose and complement loops were edge-tested (line_size = DATA_SIZE, DATA_SIZE-1, small values, multiples of 3) with all accesses provably inside `plane_data` and inside its initialized region. The `cnt_2prn = line_size_color_plane * 3 + 5` computation omits the 7 bytes emitted after the count (`\200\037`, `\000`, `\124\124`, and the count alignment), producing a wrong raster length in the printer escape stream, but this is an output-correctness issue with no memory, injection, or trust impact in this code.

assumptions: LINE_SIZE and LINE_SIZE*8 (DATA_SIZE) are compile-time constants used in fixed-size stack arrays; their exact numeric values are not shown in this snippet, but all safety arguments here depend only on the stated relationships DATA_SIZE = LINE_SIZE*8 and sizeof(plane_data) = LINE_SIZE*3, which hold for any value.

gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines writes at most line_size bytes into data; its return value is ignored, so stale bytes from a prior scan line may be reused, but the buffer is always fully defined (memset plus prior writes), so this is an output fidelity issue only.
limitations: Candidate C1 (complement loop reading beyond the region initialized by the transpose loop when line_size is not a multiple of 8) was simulated and dismissed: the lscp = (line_size/3)/3 range is always contained within the transpose-initialized region for every line_size in (DATA_SIZE-7, DATA_SIZE], so no out-of-bounds or uninitialized read is reachable.

Candidate C2: `cnt_2prn = line_size_color_plane * 3 + 5` undercounts the bytes actually emitted after the count field by 7 (the `\200\037`, `\000`, and `\124\124` bytes). This produces a malformed raster-length header in the printer output stream, but no security impact within this code; recorded as a functional bug, not a vulnerability.
No integer overflow is reachable: cnt_2prn is bounded by line_size <= DATA_SIZE, which the quoted guard enforces before any use, and cntc1/cntc2 are masks of that bounded value.

verdict.summary: Vim's bracketed_paste consumes terminal-controlled paste content and the terminal-controlled t_PE end sequence, but the dangerous buffer accumulation is provably bounded: the guard `if (end != NULL && STRLEN(end) >= NUMBUFLEN) end = NULL;` caps the end sequence length at NUMBUFLEN-1, and the `if (end[idx] == NUL) break;` arm confines the continue-path index to at most NUMBUFLEN-2, so the worst case (a maximal multibyte character written at that index) stores the trailing NUL at sizeof(buf)-2, inside `char_u buf[NUMBUFLEN + MB_MAXBYTES]`. The PASTE_EX heap copy is guarded on its only path by `if (gap != NULL && ga_grow(gap, idx + 1) == OK)`. No out-of-domain value reaches any sink; remaining corner cases (a zero-byte-producing key code coinciding with a truncated end terminator, a legacy 5/6-byte encoder, a peer withholding the end code) could not be instantiated from the given code.

assumptions: find_termcode() returns either NULL or a NUL-terminated string; the code checks NULL explicitly (`end != NULL`) and STRLEN(end) is only meaningful for a terminated string.

(*mb_char2bytes)(c, buf + idx) writes at most MB_MAXBYTES bytes for one character; this is the same constant used to size `char_u buf[NUMBUFLEN + MB_MAXBYTES]`, so the write width and the buffer slack are defined consistently by the same macro.
ga_grow(gap, n) returning OK guarantees capacity for n more items with the garray's item size (1 for byte garrays as initialized by the callers, not shown).
NUMBUFLEN and MB_MAXBYTES are the standard positive Vim macros; the bound analysis is independent of their concrete values because the guard uses the same macro that sizes the buffer.
vgetc() consumes one character per call and can return special key codes as well as normal characters; the do-while filter and the NUL/got_int break were treated as quoted control flow only.
limitations: Out-of-bounds read corner for `end[idx]`: to reach it with idx > STRLEN(end), strncmp(buf, end, idx) must return 0 with a zero byte in buf coinciding with end's terminator. That requires a vgetc() key code whose stored byte is 0 and a specifically truncated/empty t_PE value; neither producer exists in the given code (key-code definitions and t_PE setting are not shown), so the precondition is UNSOURCED.

If the active mb_char2bytes encoder could emit more than MB_MAXBYTES bytes (e.g., a legacy 5/6-byte UTF-8 arm), a one-past write of the trailing NUL becomes conceivable; such an encoder is not shown and modern Vim's encoder caps at 4 bytes, so the trigger is speculative.

Denial-of-service consideration: when t_PE is defined, the loop's empty-typeahead exit `if (end == NULL && vpeekc() == NUL) break;` never fires, so a peer that starts bracketed paste and never sends the end code keeps the loop consuming input; the quoted exit `if (c == NUL || got_int || ...) break;` still lets a typed CTRL-C interrupt it, and no corruption, retention, or amplification occurs in this code, so no vulnerability was recorded.

`ins_char_bytes(buf, idx)` can receive idx bytes that are not a single character after a partial end-sequence match followed by a mismatching byte; whether the callee mishandles that is not characterizable from the given code, and the pointer/length pair passed is inside buf's allocation on every path.

`c = buf[0];` narrows special key codes to one byte, making the `c == K_KENTER` comparison unreachable; this is a functional defect with no security consequence (cosmetic behavior in insert-paste end-of-line handling).

verdict.summary: No trigger could be instantiated for any candidate. The multi-line-match index ml_get(sub_firstlnum + nmatch - 1) is explicitly clamped by the quoted check against ml_line_count before every use on every path. The remaining candidates (needed_len cross-line arithmetic, new_start sizing vs mch_memmove/STRCAT use, stale sub_firstline) all require regmatch.endpos[0].col to exceed the length of the line where the match ends, a violation of the not-shown vim_regexec_multi contract that this code's own statements cannot produce; every sub_firstlnum adjustment path re-synchronizes the line copy before the next use.

assumptions: vim_regexec_multi reports regmatch.startpos/endpos with lnum/col inside the matched lines; this code contains no guard enforcing endpos[0].col <= STRLEN(last matched line), so needed_len = copy_len + ((unsigned)STRLEN(p1) - regmatch.endpos[0].col) + sublen + 1 relies on that unquoted callee invariant
vim_regsub_multi returns in sublen the byte length its second (output) pass will write, including the NUL; not shown
ml_get returns a valid NUL-terminated line for any in-range index; the index itself is clamped in-range by quoted code
getdigits/skip_regexp_ex/skip_substitute return well-formed pointers over the command string; failure modes not shown
limitations: needed_len underallocation candidate (lines ~801-803): trigger requires endpos[0].col > STRLEN(p1) for the last matched line, producible only if the regex engine misreports match end; not instantiable from this code, unsourced precondition

stale sub_firstline after lnum/sub_firstlnum adjustment (\n\zs path): the VIM_CLEAR(sub_firstline) plus re-fetch at sub_firstline = vim_strsave(ml_get(sub_firstlnum)) re-synchronizes before use; no divergent path found
nmatch_tl deletion bookkeeping (ml_delete loop): counts derive from the same clamped nmatch values; no over-delete path constructed
needed_len int vs unsigned new_start_len comparison uses a cast; overflow requires ~2GB line lengths bounded nowhere in this code but not constructible from its own constants

verdict.summary: This BMP decoder reads every header, colormap, and pixel value from the file (attacker-data), but each memory sink is guarded by quotable checks in execution order: colormap allocation is sized colors*4 with a read of packet_size*colors (packet_size<=4) and an exact count check; number_colors is bounded by GetBlobSize and by 1<<bits_per_pixel; the pixel buffer is allocated rows*max(bytes_per_line, columns+256) and read with an exact length/count check; all conversion strides (cases 1, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32 and the 32-bpp matte-detection loop) were recomputed and are equal to or smaller than the read stride for both even and odd column counts, including tail loops whose maximum index is columns-1; colormap index values in cases 4/8 are passed through the validating IsValidColormapIndex accessor; RLE data is decoded by a call that receives the buffer together with its usable capacity. Remaining concerns (32-bit size_t wrap in bytes_per_line arithmetic, the unvalidated index value 1 written by case 1 when the colormap has one entry, potential downstream misuse inside the unshown SyncImage/DecodeImage, and bounded ~500x file-size allocation slack) fail trigger instantiation or have impact chains that break in code not given, so they are recorded as limitations rather than findings.

assumptions: Callees not shown (ReadBlob/ReadBlobLSB* short-read semantics, SeekBlob, GetBlobSize, AcquireVirtualMemory/AcquireQuantumMemory NULL on failure, QueueAuthenticPixels row capacity of columns pixels, GetAuthenticIndexQueue capacity, IsValidColormapIndex clamping behavior on failure) are assumed to have standard ImageMagick semantics; the given code consistently checks their failure sentinels (count checks, NULL checks, offset < 0 checks) before first use.
The analysis assumes a 64-bit build (size_t/ssize_t 64-bit) for arithmetic-overflow reasoning; SetImageExtent's quoted failure check additionally bounds columns*rows by a real pixel-cache allocation.
DecodeImage is assumed to honor the capacity argument (image->columns*image->rows) it is passed; the given code's allocation (rows*max(bytes_per_line, columns+256)) is at least that capacity.

Resource limits (Magick policies) that would cap the rows*max(bytes_per_line, columns+256) allocation are not shown; the quoted length/8 > GetBlobSize check bounds it to a multiple (< ~514x) of file size, with the allocation NULL-checked.
limitations: C1 (integer wrap): on a 32-bit build, image->columns*bits_per_pixel+31 and bytes_per_line*image->rows are 32-bit size_t expressions; with columns > 2^27 and rows=1 the stride computation can wrap to a small value while the case-32 conversion uses 4*columns, producing a heap out-of-bounds read. Not confirmed: requires a 32-bit target and a ~1GB pixel-cache allocation to pass SetImageExtent; the code declares size_t-width types and the wrap is not exercised on the declared-width (64-bit) evaluation.

C2 (colormap index value): with bits_per_pixel=1 and number_colors=1, image->colors==1 but case 1 writes index values 0 and 1 into the index channel without the IsValidColormapIndex validation used in cases 4/8. The write address is in-bounds; an out-of-range colormap lookup would occur only inside the unshown SyncImage(image), whose bounds-checking behavior is not characterizable from the given code.

C7 (RLE decode): any out-of-bounds write during run-length decoding would occur inside DecodeImage, which is not shown; the given code passes the pixel buffer together with an explicit capacity (image->columns*image->rows) that fits the allocation, so the defect, if any, is not in the given statements.

C4: shifting 32-bit masks by shift counts up to 32/33 (capped by 'if (shift.red > 32U) break;') is undefined behavior in C but with fixed small shift counts and no memory-safety consequence; not classified as a vulnerability.

C6: bmp_info is memset only once outside the do-loop, so alpha_mask and color masks persist across multi-image files and can set matte=MagickTrue for a subsequent size==40 header; all resulting writes remain in-bounds, so this is a semantic (color interpretation) issue only.

verdict.summary: No exploitable vulnerability found. Every memory, index, size, and stack sink in GetEXIFProperty is guarded by an explicit check that reaches the sink in execution order and was edge-tested at 0, exactly-at-limit, one-past-limit, negative/SIZE_MAX, and truncated values: the q bounds check, the components and number_bytes overflow checks, the three dir_offset range continues, the p/tag_bytes and p/number_bytes bounds checks, the macro length clamp before every FormatLocaleString call, allocations sized from the same expression as the copy, the directory and stack-level range checks, and the signed offset range checks. The one use of p outside the tag-match block (the EXIF/GPS offset-tag read) was verified in-bounds on both of its only possible paths. Candidate OOB reads, macro buffer overflows via vsnprintf truncation returns, 32-bit wrap, stack overflow, and unbounded recursion were each simulated and shown contained at a quoted guard.

assumptions: ReadPropertyByte/ReadPropertySignedShort/ReadPropertyUnsignedShort/ReadPropertySignedLong/ReadPropertyUnsignedLong are characterized under the CALLEE BOUNDARY RULE as reads of 1/2/4 bytes with signed/unsigned interpretation; their implementations are not shown.

FormatLocaleString is characterized as vsnprintf semantics: writes at most size-1 chars plus a NUL within the destination, may return the would-be length on truncation; the macro's clamp is verified against exactly this behavior.

GetStringInfoLength/GetStringInfoDatum return the profile's byte length and base pointer; AcquireQuantumMemory returns a pointer or NULL; splay-tree operations compare stored pointer keys without dereferencing them (compare callback is NULL).

MaxTextExtent is defined outside this code; its value is not quoted here, but the buffer declaration `char buffer[MaxTextExtent]` and every clamp use the same constant, so the relative arithmetic is consistent for any value.

size_t/ssize_t are assumed at least 64-bit as declared by the platform ABI; the one 32-bit-only wrap scenario (C3) was nonetheless simulated and shown contained by the `((size_t) dir_offset+number_bytes) > length` continue.
limitations: C1 (OOB read of 4 bytes at p in the TAG_EXIF_OFFSET block when the value-block p check is skipped): could not be instantiated; both reachable p paths (p=q+8 with q <= exif+length-12, and p=exif+dir_offset with dir_offset+number_bytes <= length and number_bytes >= 5) keep the 4-byte read in bounds, and the failure arms `continue` past the block.

C2 (stack buffer overflow in EXIFMultipleValues/EXIFMultipleFractions via inflated vsnprintf return): the clamp `if (length >= (MaxTextExtent-1)) length=MaxTextExtent-1;` executes in the same iteration as the +=, so every call sees length <= MaxTextExtent-1 and a size argument >= 1; no out-of-bounds write is reachable.

C3 (32-bit number_bytes wrap): requires a 32-bit size_t not exercised by the code as written, and even then the wrapped value either fails `number_bytes < components` or fails `((size_t) dir_offset+number_bytes) > length` before any use.

C6 (infinite loop / amplification via cyclic IFD pointers): bounded by the exif_resources splay-tree deduplication (`if (GetValueFromSplayTree(exif_resources,q) == q) break;`), the stack level bound, and the per-entry `break;` after an offset-tag push; total work is linear in the profile size.

The duplicate-tag check `if (directory_stack[i].directory == (exif+tag_offset1))` compares against exif+tag_offset1 rather than the pushed exif+offset; this is an upstream functional oddity that makes parsing more restrictive (it breaks the directory scan when the current directory equals exif or exif+0x10000) but has no memory-safety consequence, since the pushed directories are range-checked and revalidated after every pop.

verdict.summary: composite_setup() processes attacker-controlled USB control-request fields (wValue, wIndex, wLength, bRequestType, bRequest) at the trust boundary, but every memory sink is guarded by quotable checks verified in execution order: wLength is clamped to USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ at entry for IN requests (and OUT requests over the limit are rejected via 'goto done'), the OS-descriptor path clamps wLength with min_t(u16, w_length, USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ) immediately before memset, copy lengths are capped with min/min_t against clamped wLength and callee-returned lengths, interface indexing is guarded by 'if (!cdev->config || intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES) break;' at all five sites, and the endpoint bit index is bounded by masks ((w_index & 0x80) >> 3) | (w_index & 0x0f) to [0,31]. Failure sentinels of lookup/parse callees (config_desc, get_string, bos_desc, fill_ext_prop, set_alt/get_alt/func_suspend returns) are tested before first use. No trigger for an out-of-bounds write, read, injection, or bypass could be instantiated; the framework-hardening clamps present in this code close the known EP0 buffer overruns.

assumptions: req->buf (cdev->req) and cdev->os_desc_req->buf are allocated with sizes matching the constants USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ and USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ respectively; the constant names and their sole use as clamps for writes into those buffers are the basis, since the allocations are not shown in the given code.
MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES bounds the interface[] array of struct usb_configuration; the guard 'intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES' at each indexing site relies on that kernel definition.
f->endpoints bitmap is at least 32 bits wide so test_bit(endp, ...) with endp masked to [0,31] is in range; the declaration is in the gadget framework header, not in the given code.

count_ext_prop/len_ext_prop/fill_ext_prop operate on properties registered by the gadget driver at bind time (not attacker-settable through any statement in this code) and return lengths consistent with what they wrote into buf.
limitations: Function-driver callbacks (f->set_alt, f->get_alt, f->func_suspend, f->get_status, f->setup, f->req_match) and configuration helpers (config_desc, get_string, bos_desc, device_qual, count_ext_prop, len_ext_prop, fill_ext_prop) are not shown; if any mishandles the attacker-controlled wIndex/wValue passed to it, the defect would be in that callee. This code passes raw protocol fields consistent with the framework convention (comments document that functions handle their interfaces) and checks returned error sentinels before consuming them, so no defect is attributable to these call sites.

Hypothetical integer overflow of 'int count' in the OS-descriptor RECIP_INTERFACE branch would require count_ext_prop/len_ext_prop to return near INT_MAX; count derives from gadget-registered (trusted) properties, so the precondition is not attacker-instantiable from this code.

The deliberate const cast writing cpu_to_le16(USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ) into ctrl->wLength writes only a fixed constant and is documented by the adjacent comment ('we are going to overwrite on purpose'); it carries no attacker-controlled content.

verdict.summary: No memory-safety or injection defect demonstrable in the given code. The only attacker-sized write (the argument copy loop) is preceded by mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2), a characterizable callee that sizes the stack for exactly the slots written; remaining candidates depend on code not shown.

assumptions: mrb_stack_extend extends the fiber stack to accommodate at least len+2 slots from stbase (mruby core semantics); its internals are not in the given code.
fiber_check, fiber_check_cfunc, fiber_result, mrb_vm_exec are not shown; their behavior is assumed per mruby semantics.
c->status, c->ci, c->stbase, c->cibase have no assignments in the given code (UNSOURCED).

verdict.summary: In the multi-frame animation path (DimFlag==16 with Frames>=2), the MAT decoder frees the scanline buffer and sets BImgBuff=NULL, then jumps back to the NEXT_FRAME label. The only allocation of BImgBuff lies above that label, so on every subsequent frame the raster loop calls ReadBlob(image2,ldblk,(unsigned char *)BImgBuff) with a NULL (freed) destination and attacker-controlled ldblk>0, causing a NULL-pointer write and process crash. The trigger (Frames>=2, SizeX>=1, pixel bytes present) is fully attacker-controlled through the parsed image file, so an untrusted image crashes the decoding process (denial of service).

evidence.reason: After RelinquishMagickMemory(BImgBuff) and BImgBuff = NULL (lines 258-259), the frame counter read from the file (Frames = ReadBlobXXXLong(image2)) controls this backward jump to NEXT_FRAME. The only allocation of BImgBuff (AcquireQuantumMemory((size_t)(ldblk),sizeof(double))) executes before the NEXT_FRAME label and is skipped on re-entry, so the freed/NULL buffer is reused.

Sink: on the second and later frames reached via goto NEXT_FRAME, BImgBuff is NULL (set by 'BImgBuff = NULL;' after RelinquishMagickMemory) and ldblk >= 1 (SizeX >= 1 enforced by 'if (image->columns == 0 || image->rows == 0) goto MATLAB_KO;'), so ReadBlob copies attacker-supplied scanline bytes into a NULL destination. The guard 'if (BImgBuff == NULL)' exists only at the original allocation site above the NEXT_FRAME label and is bypassed by the goto; no NULL check, re-allocation, or error arm exists on any path between the label and this use. This is a use of freed memory / NULL-pointer write (CWE-416/CWE-476) triggered solely by attacker-controlled file content (Frames>=2, DimFlag==16, z==1, any supported CellType, SizeY rows of pixel data).

assumptions: ReadBlob's semantics are taken as documented: it copies up to count bytes from the blob into the provided data pointer; with data==NULL and count>0 this writes to a NULL destination (characterizable standard-library-style behavior of the ImageMagick blob layer).
GetAuthenticPixels on a correctly-sized image (SetImageExtent succeeded) returns a valid pixel queue, so the first loop iteration reaches the ReadBlob sink on re-entry frames.
limitations: ldblk integer wrap (e.g. ldblk = 4*SizeX overflowing to negative for SizeX near 2^29) would shrink the allocation, but such columns must first pass SetImageExtent(image,image->columns,image->rows,exception), whose failure returns DestroyImageList; the trigger is not instantiable from this code's statements.

InsertComplexDoubleRow/InsertComplexFloatRow are called with row index i up to SizeY-1 on an image whose rows became SizeX after RotateImage(image, 90.0, ...) (columns/rows are swapped); when SizeY > SizeX the row index is out of the image's row domain, but the callees are not shown and their bounds behavior cannot be characterized, so the impact chain breaks there (possible secondary defect).

The frame counter Frames is an attacker-controlled 32-bit value bounding the 'while(--Frames>0) goto NEXT_FRAME' loop; each iteration performs allocation-heavy work (RotateImage, AcquireNextImage, AcquireQuantumInfo) largely independent of file size, giving an attacker-scalable resource-consumption vector (CWE-400), secondary to the confirmed NULL-use defect.

Partially-uninitialized EndianIndicator/identific reads at exact EOF are guarded by 'ReadBlob(image,124,...) != 124' and 'ReadBlob(image,2,...) != 2' checks plus EOFBlob tests, so no uninitialized data reaches a sink.

verdict.summary: Analysis of this glob() revision found no instantiated vulnerability. Every allocation/copy pair is sized from the same expression as the copy (dirname: malloc(dirlen+1) vs mempcpy(newp, pattern, dirlen); tilde: malloc(home_len+dirlen) vs mempcpy chain of home_len+dirlen bytes with the source NUL riding at the last index; user home: malloc(home_len+rest_len+1) vs home_len+rest_len copy plus explicit *d='\0'; GLOB_MARK: realloc(strlen+2) vs a 2-byte write at offset len-2; brace: onealt of strlen(pattern)-1 bytes vs a maximum write of prefix+alternative+suffix+1 <= strlen(pattern)-1 since '{', '}' and skipped alternatives reduce length by at least 2). The realloc growth is guarded by the quoted and boundary-correct check 'if (newcount > SIZE_MAX / sizeof (char *) - 2)', which keeps (newcount+2)*sizeof(char*) <= SIZE_MAX-7. The strcpy at the GLOB_MARK site is bounded by construction. Control-flow analysis of the dirs lifecycle found no double-free or use of the uninitialized dirs struct: every path to globfree(&dirs) passes through the 'status = glob (dirname, ..., &dirs)' call, and the callee's error paths NULL the vector before returning statuses that bypass our cleanup. Each 'if (malloc_dirname) free (dirname)' is paired with an explicit reset or reassignment of the ownership flag. This revision contains the historically known glibc glob fixes (GLOB_TILDE sizing and GLOB_BRACE off-by-one), and no candidate's trigger could be instantiated with a sourced precondition.

assumptions: glob_use_alloca and alloca_account internals are not shown; the alloca size cap is assumed to exist in the callee. This does not create an unchecked sink because every alloca arm in this code has a quoted malloc fallback with a NULL test (e.g., 'newp = malloc (dirlen + 1); if (newp == NULL) return GLOB_NOSPACE;').

next_brace_sub, glob_in_dir, prefix_array, is_dir, __glob_pattern_type, scratch_buffer_grow, and collated_compare are not shown; their behavior was only relied on where this code quotes the handling of their failure sentinels (NULL / 0 / nonzero checks) before first use.

getenv("HOME"), __getlogin_r, and getpwnam_r return external configuration data; all their NULL / empty / error sentinels are tested before use in the given code ('if (home_dir == NULL || home_dir[0] == \'\0\')', 'if (err == 0)', 'if (p != NULL)', scratch_buffer_grow NULL handling).
This is the post-fix glibc revision: the known historical GLOB_TILDE buffer overflow and GLOB_BRACE off-by-one are already corrected in the quoted arithmetic.
limitations: Candidate 'brace expansion off-by-one (glob CVE family)' dismissed: recomputed maximum write count (begin-pattern)+(next-p)+(strlen(++rest)+1) is strictly <= strlen(pattern)-1 for all brace forms including the empty-alternative edge ('a{}b' simulated: 3 bytes written into a 3-byte buffer), so the trigger's harmful value lies outside the reachable range.

Candidate 'integer overflow in (newcount+2)*sizeof(char*)' dismissed: the quoted guard admits only newcount <= SIZE_MAX/8-2, for which the product is at most SIZE_MAX-7; boundary value simulated, no wrap.

Candidate 'uninitialized dirs.gl_pathv reaching globfree(&dirs) at no_matches' dismissed on control flow: the only routes into that block execute 'status = glob (dirname, ..., &dirs)' first, and the recursive call's error paths NULL gl_pathv before any status that skips the cleanup; the two early 'goto no_matches' sites are preceded by 'dirs.gl_pathv = NULL;'.
Candidate 'strcpy use (CWE-676)' dismissed: the write target '&new[len - 2]' with len = strlen(...)+2 places exactly the 2 written bytes at the end of a len-byte allocation; bounded by construction.

Candidate 'attacker-controlled recursion depth via nested braces or pattern/' dismissed: each recursive call strictly reduces the pattern (a brace group is consumed, or the directory prefix is stripped), so depth is bounded linearly by pattern length with no exponential amplification in this function.

verdict.summary: eval_string() sizes its output buffer in a first scan and fills it in a second; an exhaustive mirror of every escape class (simple escapes, hex/unicode, octal, multibyte, special-key forms, interpolation brace pairs) shows the second pass never writes more than the first pass reserves. The only structurally dangerous input for the second pass, a backslash immediately before the string terminator, is rejected by the first pass before any allocation. The post-write boundary check uses the corrected >= comparison. Remaining candidates (int truncation of len on gigabyte-scale literals, trans_special exceeding its documented bound, detection-only iemsg) all rest on unsourced preconditions and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: The caller positions *arg consistent with the off/interpolate contract (opening quote present for non-interpolate, consumed for interpolate); the given code does not document this, but no path within the code depends on a violation.

find_special_key and trans_special succeed/fail consistently for identical inputs and flags, and their output never exceeds the 9 bytes the code's own comment documents; their internal behavior is not shown.
(*mb_char2bytes) writes at most 6 bytes for any input value, per the documented encoding semantics referenced by the \u and \U cases.
limitations: len = (int)(p - *arg + extra) would truncate on a string literal near or above INT_MAX scale (extra grows by 5 per \< form), potentially yielding a small allocation filled by the copy loop; instantiating this requires a roughly 1GB literal to reach *arg, and no statement in this code produces, permits, or bounds such input, so the precondition is unsourced.

The check if (end >= rettv->vval.v_string + len) iemsg(...) is detection-only: it does not stop subsequent writes. If trans_special ever exceeded the 9-byte documented maximum the accounting would fail open with a heap overflow; this depends entirely on unshown callee behavior and could not be instantiated from the given code.

find_special_key's pointer advancement on the failure path (returns 0) is not characterizable from the given code; both loops call the same parser with the same flags at the same position, so any divergence there would be a callee defect, not one in this code.

nr = (nr << 4) + hex2nr(*p) with 8 hex digits (\U case) invokes signed int overflow (UB) for values at or above 0x08000000, but the subsequent write is bounded at 6 bytes against a 10-byte consumed span, so no memory-safety consequence was instantiated.

The octal escape \0 writes an embedded NUL byte, which truncates the resulting Vim string as seen by downstream consumers; this is a known language semantic, not a memory-safety defect, and no downstream misuse is shown.

verdict.summary: ReadTIFFImage validates every tag-derived value that reaches a memory, size, or index sink: bits_per_sample is range-checked (<=0 or >32 rejected except IEEEFP/64), samples_per_pixel is capped at MaxPixelChannels, scanline_size is checked for <=0 and against 1.5*number_pixels before the pixel buffer is allocated from the same expression, every allocation's NULL result is checked before use, rows_per_strip is clamped to image->rows, tile dimensions pass tag-presence, resource-limit, and HeapOverflowSanityCheck guards before the tile buffer is sized by the same expression the reads use, and the colormap loop is bounded by image->colors = 2^bits_per_sample which matches libtiff's documented colormap array size under the MaxColormapSize gate. The remaining edge cases (rows_per_strip==0 or zero tile dimensions yielding a zero-sized strip/tile buffer and a SIZE_MAX wrap of rows_remaining, extreme-dimension overflow of the extent products, a possible NULL index queue in ReadYCCKMethod) cannot be instantiated from this code alone: producing a zero RowsPerStrip or zero tile dimension through TIFFGetField depends on libtiff's unshown tag validation, the extent wrap requires resource limits and pixel-cache allocations this code itself checks and would fail, and the YCCK method selection happens inside an unshown callee. None of these is a confirmed vulnerability in this code; they are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: libtiff delivers TIFFTAG_COLORMAP as three arrays of 2^BitsPerSample uint16 entries, TIFFTAG_WHITEPOINT as 2 floats, TIFFTAG_PRIMARYCHROMATICITIES as 6 floats, and TIFFTAG_EXTRASAMPLES as (count, array of count uint16) per its documented tag semantics; the colormap, chromaticity, and sample_info loops are in-bounds under those documented semantics.
AcquireVirtualMemory, AcquireQuantumMemory, and AcquireQuantumInfo return NULL on failure or size overflow, and every such result is NULL-checked in this code before use.
SetImageExtent enforces width/height resource limits and pixel-cache allocation, failing for dimensions whose cache cannot be allocated; its failure path is checked in this code.

TIFFReadEncodedStrip, TIFFReadTile, and TIFFReadPixels write at most the size passed by this code (TIFFStripSize, bounded by the allocated extent; the scanline path is bounded by the checked scanline_size).
This coder is invoked on untrusted TIFF file content; all tag values retrieved via TIFFGetField/TIFFGetFieldDefaulted are treated as attacker-data.

ThrowReaderException, RelinquishVirtualMemory, RelinquishMagickMemory, and DestroyQuantumInfo follow standard framework semantics (free and return NULL); ThrowTIFFException re-nulls pixel_info and destroys quantum_info, preventing double frees.
limitations: C1: If TIFFGetField(TIFFTAG_ROWSPERSTRIP) could return 1 with rows_per_strip==0, then extent=4*(samples_per_pixel+1)*TIFFStripSize(tiff) would be 0 and rows_remaining-- in ReadStripMethod would wrap to SIZE_MAX, causing ImportQuantumPixels to read heap memory out of bounds from an undersized strip_pixels buffer (the guard 'if (rows_per_strip > (uint32) image->rows) rows_per_strip=(uint32) image->rows;' clamps only from above; a zero check for rows_per_strip exists nowhere in this code). Not instantiated: whether libtiff's directory reader can store and deliver a zero RowsPerStrip (and whether AcquireQuantumMemory(0,1) returns non-NULL) is unshown, specific tag-validation behavior of the library that cannot be characterized as a generic documented semantic. UNSOURCED precondition: libtiff accepting RowsPerStrip==0.

C2: If TIFFTAG_TILEWIDTH/TILELENGTH could be 0, the quoted guards (TIFFGetField presence checks, AcquireMagickResource(Width/HeightResource,...), HeapOverflowSanityCheck(rows,...)) would not reject 0, giving extent==0, an undersized tile_pixels buffer, and a non-advancing 'for (y=0; y < (ssize_t) image->rows; y+=rows)' loop. Same unshown-producer contingency as C1. UNSOURCED precondition: libtiff accepting zero tile dimensions.

C3: The extent products 4*(samples_per_pixel+1)*TIFFStripSize(tiff) and 4*(samples_per_pixel+1)*MagickMax(rows*TIFFTileRowSize(tiff),TIFFTileSize(tiff)) can wrap size_t only at roughly 2^64/132-scale strip/tile dimensions; reaching them requires SetImageExtent (whose failure is checked in this code) or AcquireMagickResource limit values (UNSOURCED configuration) to accept ~4e9-scale dimensions, and libtiff's own signed 64-bit strip-size arithmetic at those scales is uncharacterizable. Trigger not instantiated.

C4: ReadYCCKMethod dereferences 'SetPixelBlack(indexes+x,...)' with indexes from GetAuthenticIndexQueue(image); whether method selection in GetJPEGMethod (callee not shown) can choose ReadYCCKMethod for an image without an index channel cannot be determined from this code.

C5: image->page.x/y are computed from image->x_resolution/image->y_resolution which are set only if the XRESOLUTION/YRESOLUTION tags exist; when only XPOSITION/YPOSITION exist, the members hold AcquireImage's initialization (not shown). Impact is limited to page-offset values; no memory-safety or security-state consequence.
C7: The return value of TIFFReadPhotoshopLayers(image_info,image,exception) is ignored; the callee is not shown and no consequence can be characterized from this code.

verdict.summary: hfsplus_block_allocate leaks the kmap mapping and the page-cache reference when allocation fails: the early-exit path at the found: label (start >= size) jumps to out while the page is still kmap'd, and no path in the function ever calls put_page on the page acquired by read_mapping_page. Every call on a crafted filesystem metadata state (attacker-controlled size/offset/bitmap content) permanently pins a page-cache page and, on highmem systems, a kmap slot, enabling attacker-scalable memory/kmap exhaustion denial of service via repeated allocation calls on a mounted malicious HFS+ image.

evidence.reason: The early-exit path jumps to out while the page acquired at line 17 (read_mapping_page) and mapped at line 22 (kmap(page)) is still kmap'd and referenced; no kunmap or put_page exists on this path. With attacker-controlled size=1000, offset=2000 and a zero bitmap page, start=2000 >= size triggers the leak on every allocation attempt.
The out label releases only the mutex; no kunmap(page) or put_page(page) is performed, so the mapping and reference held on entry to the found: early-exit path (lines 79-81) are permanently leaked.

read_mapping_page acquires a page reference and kmap(page) acquires a mapping; the function contains no put_page anywhere, so the reference leaks on every non-error return as well, pinning page-cache memory with attacker-scalable repetition.

assumptions: PAGE_CACHE_BITS equals PAGE_CACHE_SIZE*8 (4096-byte cache pages => 32768 bits); the code uses it only as a constant mask.

read_mapping_page returns a page with an elevated reference that callers must release with put_page, and kmap must be paired with kunmap (characterizable standard kernel API semantics per the callee boundary rule).

Callers pass size/offset/len values derived from on-disk HFS+ metadata (volume header, catalog, bitmap file), i.e., untrusted content from a mounted filesystem image per the data-origin rule.

verdict.summary: Systematic taint tracing of every attacker-controlled TIFF tag through all decoding paths (YCCK, strip, tile, generic) found each memory sink bounded by guards quoted in execution order: the samples_per_pixel and bits_per_sample gates, the rows_per_strip clamp to image->rows, the 1.5x scanline-to-buffer check, HeapOverflowSanityCheck before size-derived allocations, and buffers allocated from the same expressions that bound the subsequent pointer walks (strip: extent >= 4*bytes_per_sample*(spp+1)*TIFFStripSize while p advances at most rows_per_strip*stride == TIFFStripSize per strip, with p reset per refill; tile: extent >= 4*(spp+1)*rows*TIFFTileRowSize bounding the per-plane walk; generic: allocation exactly columns*rows matching the walk). Boundary values (0, exact-fit, one-past-limit) were tested and remain in range; degenerate zero-dimension cases are cut off by quoted NULL/break checks before any dereference, and rows_per_strip==0 collapses extent to 0 so the allocation NULL check catches it. Residual concerns (zero tile length, 32-bit extent overflow, CastDoubleToLong on extreme resolution products, JPEG method selection in GetJPEGMethod) depend on libtiff directory validation and MagickCore helpers not shown, which per the trigger-proof rules could not be instantiated.

assumptions: Standard libtiff semantics relied on per the callee boundary rule: TIFFStripSize == TIFFVStripSize(tiff, rows_per_strip) == rows_per_strip * one-row size; TIFFTileSize == tile rows * TIFFTileRowSize; TIFFReadEncodedStrip/TIFFReadTile return -1 on error; TIFFTAG_WHITEPOINT provides 2 floats and TIFFTAG_PRIMARYCHROMATICITIES 6 floats per TIFF 6.0 spec; colormap arrays provide 2^bits_per_sample entries.

MagickCore helpers characterized by documented semantics: AcquireVirtualMemory/AcquireQuantumMemory return NULL on failure or zero count; HeapOverflowSanityCheck rejects multiplication overflow; ClampToQuantum saturates; GetAuthenticPixels/QueueAuthenticPixels return NULL for out-of-cache or zero-extent requests.

MaxColormapSize and QuantumRange are build-constant macros; the colormap path is gated by pow(2.0,1.0*bits_per_sample) <= MaxColormapSize which bounds image->colors to the libtiff colormap array length.
limitations: Tile path with TIFFTAG_TILELENGTH == 0 would make 'for (y=0; y < rows; y+=rows)' non-terminating; could not instantiate because a usable tile directory with zero tile length is rejected by libtiff directory validation not shown in this code.

extent computations such as 4*((image->depth+7)/8)*(samples_per_pixel+1)*TIFFStripSize(tiff) could overflow 32-bit size_t; the code's declared size_t/MagickSizeType widths indicate 64-bit targets, so this wrap is not exercised by the code as written.

image->page.x=CastDoubleToLong(ceil(x_position*image->x_resolution-0.5)) can receive extreme or NaN float tag values; CastDoubleToLong is not shown and the consequence is a page-offset metadata value, so no memory or security-state impact was instantiated.

ReadYCCKMethod safety rests only on the quoted 1.5x scanline check and the allocation pixel_info=AcquireVirtualMemory(number_pixels,sizeof(uint32)), independent of how GetJPEGMethod (not shown) selects the method; even a degenerate spp==1 selection stays within the buffer at the exact boundary (columns*4 == number_pixels*4 minimum), so no out-of-bounds access was instantiated.

rows_per_strip == 0 from a hostile TIFFTAG_ROWSPERSTRIP would make TIFFStripSize 0 and extent 0, so AcquireQuantumMemory(0, sizeof) returns NULL and the quoted NULL check catches it; an inconsistent libtiff state with rows_per_strip==0 but nonzero strip size could not be characterized from the given code.
